THE FILM / 0:48

How it works

The film as text
  1. Card. The Cashu Card is an NFC smart card that runs an open protocol.
  2. Key. The card makes its key on the chip, and the key stays there.
  3. Load. A wallet writes eight pieces of ecash into the card's 128 slots.
  4. Tap. The till is offline. It selects the card and names the pieces for a 21 sat bill.
  5. Sign. The card signs once for the whole payment and burns the pieces it signed for.
  6. Settle. The till accepts the payment offline. Later, it settles with the mint.
ONE TAP / SIX STEPS

One tap, step by step

  1. The customer holds the card to the back of the merchant's phone, and the phone selects the Cashu Card applet.

  2. The phone reads the card's pieces and names the ones it wants for a 21 sat bill: 1, 4 and 16 sat.

  3. The phone sends the outputs it will swap those pieces for at the mint.

  4. The card signs once for the whole payment and burns each piece it signed for.

  5. The phone checks the mint's signature on each piece offline, then accepts the payment. Until it settles, the merchant carries the risk that a piece was spent elsewhere.

  6. The card leaves the phone. Later, back online, the phone swaps the pieces at the mint and the payment settles.

EXPERIMENTAL / BEFORE YOU LOAD A CARD

Risks to know

Cashu Card is an experimental open source project. It runs NUT-CCP, a draft NUT with little testing or review outside this project. Keep only small amounts on a card, amounts you can afford to lose.

  • A lost card loses its balance. The key that spends the card's ecash lives only on its chip, and a backup cannot recreate it.
  • The mint backs the ecash. A card's ecash is a claim on one mint. If that mint fails, the ecash loses its value.
  • The owner key needs a backup. The wallet that set the card up holds its owner key. Without it, a blocked PIN stays blocked and a large balance can be stranded.
  • Three wrong PINs block the card. Any reader in range can send them. The owner's wallet sets a new PIN.
  • Any reader can read the card. Its balance and history are readable without the PIN. Spending takes the chip's signature, within the owner's limits.
  • Offline payments carry risk for the merchant. Until a till settles with the mint, the merchant carries the risk that a piece was spent elsewhere first.
  • Testing is limited. The applet has run end to end on NXP J3R180 cards with a few named phones, as the 23 October report records. Tests on silicon for a card pulled mid-write and for timing attacks, and an independent security review, are still to come. The security model lists every open item.
CARDS / NXP J3R180

Where to get cards

The Cashu Card applet runs on NXP J3R180 cards (JCOP 4, Java Card 3.0.5) with contact and contactless interfaces. Buy them unfused and initialized, with the default GlobalPlatform keys, then install the applet from a phone or a computer.

01 / FOR TESTING

A few blank cards

This Amazon listing names the dual interface and the default SCP02 keys. A few cards are enough to try the protocol with a phone or a desk reader.

SETUP / CASHU CARD APPLET

Install the applet

A blank card needs the Cashu Card applet before it can hold ecash. Install it from a phone or from a computer.

01 / WITH A PHONE

1.0.0 beta for iPhone and Android
